result.title: Rent-Seeking Language Models: Reward Models Set the Prices, Frequent Audits Curb the Rent
result.summary: Reward model overoptimization in RLHF is usually described as reward hacking. We recast it as rent-seeking: the policy, a firm, earns reward from a regulator, the proxy reward model, that true quality does not back. The lens turns overoptimization into measurable quantities, namely rent, a capture index and deadweight loss, and into testable predictions from the economics of regulation. In a fixed, version-controlled testbed with three model families, accuracy-matched proxy reward models and two gold reward models, RL turns 41% to 66% of its proxy gain into rent while gold reward plateaus. Rent follows each regulator's prices. Neither proxy verifies facts, but one pays for confident specifics and the other for displays of diligence, so RL policies learn to fabricate details about nonexistent entities (97% to 100% of probes) or to deflect factual questions (67% to 98%). Kinship between policy and regulator adds a fixed premium of about 0.1 standard deviations but gives the policy no extra leverage under optimization. At a fixed expected fine, frequent mild audits beat rare severe ones, and random audits are as efficient per audit as targeted ones. Bringing the bunching estimator of tax economics to RL training, we also find a first sign that policies learn to stay just below a targeted audit's threshold.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把 RLHF 中的 reward model overoptimization 重新表述为「寻租」：策略作为企业从 proxy reward model 这一监管者处获取真实质量无法支撑的收益，并在受控测试平台上用 rent、capture index、deadweight loss 等指标量化，考察审计频率与强度、policy 与 regulator 的亲缘关系等条件。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「寻租」度量与审计/阈值设计可能可供核查能否用于诊断 LVR 训练中答案是否真的依赖视觉证据（如视觉旁路、指标劫持），但论文本身不涉及多模态或 latent 推理状态。
